subject: Using ho2.hpp as a template for functions involving numerical solution of ODEs

messages.author: 5a7d96b840c23bef
messages.subject: Using ho2.hpp as a template for functions involving numerical solution of ODEs
parts:
I'm trying to use ho2.hpp (https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/wiki/ODE-Integrator-Support) as a template for other functions involving numerical solution of ODEs. I'm stuck on how to generalize the example to models with a vector of parameters (rather than a single scalar parameter). In particular I would like to know how to appropriately structure the return value to contain the ODE solution and the precomputed gradient. ho2.hpp generates the return value with

      for (int n = 0; n < t.size(); n++) 
        for (int m = 0; m < x0.size(); m++) {
          x_return(n,m) 
            = stan::agrad::var(new stan::agrad::precomp_v_vari(x(n,m), gamma.vi_, x(n,m+x0.size())));
        }
      return x_return;
    }

but precomp_v_vari appears to be appropriate only for derivatives with respect to a scalar variable. 

Thanks,
Bill

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Using ho2.hpp as a template for functions involving numerical solution of ODEs
parts:
Autodiff vectors and matrices (and arrays) are just collections
of autodiff scalars. So what's going on in the code below
is that x_return is a matrix and its entries are getting populated
with gradients. If you need richer gradients, you need to replace
precomp_v_vari. In general, you can just use Stan operations and
they produce the right output and gradients --- you only need to
worry about something more complicated if you want to partially
evaluate (i.e., unfold) the derivative calcs.

If you really want examples of how to do that efficiently, look
at some .hpp files in stan/agrad/rev/matrix/.

On the good news front, I've finished writing functions, and will
write a general ODE solver that encapsulates all of this behind the
scenes based on the system function.

- Bob
